authority: Record Clearing Implementation Authority Reconciled (2026-08-24), Completed Decision Matrix — decisions that govern a single route

timing.anchorText: no fixed elapsed period; relief unlocks on a qualifying record plus facts sufficient to establish the statutory trafficking nexus

Conduct occurred during trafficking and would not have occurred but for trafficking
Proof by preponderance
routes.packetFamily: Alabama Trafficking-Victim Expungement Petition under §§ 15-27-1(a)(8) / 15-27-2(a)(8)
routes.notes: Do not apply the general 90-day, one-year, three-year, five-year, or pardoned-felony Alabama periods to this branch. Contested nexus or excluded-offense analysis is a legal-aid or attorney referral, not a checkout.

routes.mechanism: Cannabis conviction erasure — petition branch outside the automatic date window

timing.anchorText: no general elapsed wait; eligibility is unlocked by the offense, conviction date, quantity, and statutory category

exclusions: Exact cannabis statute, conviction date, quantity/conduct, and automatic-versus-petition category
routes.packetFamily: Connecticut Cannabis Erasure Petition
packetComponents: Petition under the applicable cannabis-erasure provision
routes.notes: Automatic erasure covers § 21a-279(c) convictions entered from 2000-01-01 through 2015-09-30; that cohort files nothing and must never share this checkout path. Ask whether the record should already have been erased before offering this petition.

timing.anchorText: three, five, or seven years from the statutory completion or discharge anchor, according to the discretionary category; favorable-termination and automatic branches carry no elapsed filing wait

processingDeadlines.label: Attorney General 120-day response window
processingDeadlines.note: post-filing procedure under § 1017; never a participant waiting period

exclusions: Juvenile record classified under §§ 1017, 1017A, or 1018
Category-specific offense and adjudication limits satisfied
routes.packetFamily: Delaware Juvenile Expungement Petition under 10 Del. C. §§ 1017 / 1018
routes.notes: § 1017 favorable-termination matters are mandatory with no elapsed wait; § 1017A eligible records run through the automatic program with a petition or correction path only where the automatic process did not occur. The three-year value here is the lowest discretionary § 1018 branch; the five- and seven-year branches turn on the offense category, which the intake must collect.

routes.mechanism: Cannabis expungement — petition branch for a qualifying pending or petition-eligible matter

timing.anchorText: event-specific petition eligibility under the cannabis subsection; not a general sealing wait

exclusions: Minor-cannabis offense within statutory quantity/date limits and the correct nonconviction, supervision, conviction, or pending-case category
routes.packetFamily: Illinois Cannabis Expungement Petition under 20 ILCS 2630/5.2
routes.notes: The automatic cohort (minor-cannabis nonconviction, supervision and qualified-probation records, including the one-year-from-arrest trigger where the statute uses it) receives status and correction guidance, not a paid petition. Conviction records follow the executive-clemency pardon-to-expungement process and must be labelled as a clemency application, not a routine court packet. Do not borrow Illinois's general supervision, misdemeanor, felony, or first-offender sealing periods.

timing.anchorText: available immediately upon successful completion of the qualifying specialty-court program; no additional elapsed period applies

exclusions: Participant successfully completed a qualifying specialty court and the conviction is otherwise within the statutory expungement scope
routes.packetFamily: Kansas Specialty-Court Expungement Petition under § 21-6614

supersedes.note: the ordinary three-year conviction period, which § 21-6614 expressly permits this branch to bypass

routes.notes: The ordinary three-year clock must not be applied here, and must still apply to every non-specialty-court branch.

routes.mechanism: Misdemeanor expungement after an Article 894(B) set-aside and dismissal
routes.statute: La. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 894(B) and 977

timing.anchorText: event-triggered by entry of the Article 894(B) set-aside and dismissal after successful completion of the deferred sentence or probation

exclusions: Misdemeanor disposed under Article 894(B), with all statutory Article 977 eligibility and exclusion rules satisfied
routes.packetFamily: Louisiana Article 977 Misdemeanor Expungement Packet

supersedes.note: the separate Article 977 five-year clean-period route, which is not this route's waiting period

routes.notes: Do not attach the five-year alternative route or the DWI-diversion arrest-date clock unless independently applicable.

routes.mechanism: Felony expungement on a first-offender pardon

timing.anchorText: unlocked by the valid first-offender pardon, which arises on sentence completion and payment of court costs; the pardon itself is not a waiting-period rule

Excluded offenses and other statutory restrictions still apply
routes.packetFamily: Louisiana Article 978 First-Offender-Pardon Expungement Packet
routes.notes: The product must verify the pardon rather than infer it from a completion date. No additional five- or ten-year clean period unless the person is using one of those independent Article 978 routes.

routes.mechanism: Felony expungement after an Article 893(E) set-aside and dismissal

exclusions: Felony disposed under Article 893(E) and otherwise eligible under Article 978, including all offense exclusions
routes.packetFamily: Louisiana Article 978 Felony Expungement Packet

routes.notes: Do not reuse Article 978's alternative clean-period routes as a mandatory wait for an 893(E) dismissal.

routes.mechanism: Police-record expungement where no charge was filed, pre-October 1, 2007 arrests

timing.anchorText: a written request to the police agency, which must be made within eight years of the incident; the eight years is a filing deadline that bars a late request, not a waiting period before filing

processingDeadlines.label: 60-day agency processing period
processingDeadlines.note: agency processing after the request; never displayed as a participant wait

requiredFacts: Confirmation no charge was ever filed?
exclusions: No charging document was filed
Police-record relief only
Incident date determines request versus automatic process

packetComponents: Written request to the law-enforcement agency
routes.notes: For an arrest or detention on or after October 1, 2007 with no charge filed, § 10-103.1 requires automatic expungement within the statutory agency period; if the automatic action did not occur, give agency correction and escalation guidance rather than a court packet unless the statute's review mechanism is invoked.

routes.mechanism: Juvenile sealing — petition branch for serious and OUI matters

Murder/Class A-B-C/OUI for petition
Category-specific clean-record conditions

routes.notes: Qualifying Class D, Class E and civil-type juvenile matters enter the automatic branch with no separate participant filing wait. The three-year petition branch is limited to murder, Class A, B or C juvenile crimes and OUI matters.

exclusions: Conviction under the covered prostitution statutes or corresponding ordinance
Direct-result trafficking nexus
Statutory proof requirements

routes.notes: Narrower than a general trafficking-based set-aside: limited to the covered prostitution statutes or corresponding ordinances. Contested or noncovered offenses are a referral, not a checkout. Do not broaden the route on pending 2025-2026 legislation that has not become law.

timing.anchorText: termination of the deferred sentence with the qualifying dismissal or confidentiality order; there is no additional elapsed eligibility period

exclusions: Valid Montana deferred sentence successfully completed
Statutory dismissal/confidentiality conditions satisfied
routes.notes: Do not add a general expungement clock after the deferred sentence terminates. The product verifies the deferred-sentence order, successful completion, dismissal, and whether CRISS or court confidentiality already occurred, and offers a limited court or agency packet only where one is actually required.

timing.anchorText: no elapsed waiting period; removal or confidentiality is required on a qualifying no-charge or nonconviction disposition, or on invalidation of a conviction

exclusions: Montana criminal-history information within § 44-5-202 and eligible for removal/confidentiality
Operational branch depends on record date and whether automatic action occurred
routes.notes: For qualifying records arising after the July 1, 2017 operational change, CRISS should process removal automatically; if the record remains, give a correction request and escalation path. Do not sell a court-expungement packet unless a separate court order is actually required.

exclusions: Offense before December 1, 2019 at age 16 or 17
Covered misdemeanor/Class H or I felony
Statutory exclusions absent

routes.notes: Limited to offences committed before December 1, 2019 while the person was sixteen or seventeen, within the covered misdemeanor or Class H/I felony categories and outside the motor-vehicle, impaired-driving, registrable-sex and other exclusions. Do not borrow the waiting periods in §§ 15A-145 or 15A-145.5.

exclusions: Conviction has actually been vacated
Use the special vacatur provision rather than ordinary offense-class annulment clocks

routes.notes: Require the actual vacatur order; a claimed appeal or collateral challenge is not enough. Do not import the ordinary offense-class waiting periods into this branch. The on-or-after 2019-01-01 cohort is automatic and files nothing.

timing.anchorText: available on the qualifying reversal, dismissal, nolle prosequi, successful diversion or conditional discharge, acquittal or other listed disposition, with the required documentation and no filing wait; the separate arrest-with-no-felony-charge affidavit branch requires a showing that no felony charge was filed during the year after arrest

routes.notes: The one-year condition is a substantive lookback for the arrest-with-no-felony-charge branch, not a universal waiting period.

routes.mechanism: Set-aside of arrests or charges without conviction

Correct no-instrument versus acquittal/dismissal branch
Statutory exclusions absent

Offense class and date are mandatory intake facts for that fallback.
